What happened (direct)


Your local main is behind remote


You successfully pushed the tag


But main branch push was rejected


So:


builder-ui-stable tag = ✅ already on remote


main = ❌ not updated yet



Correct fix (safe, no history break)
Bashgit pull origin main --rebase
git push origin main

If rebase produces conflicts
Run:
Bashgit status
Fix files → then:
Bashgit add .
git rebase --continue
git push origin main

DO NOT do this


do NOT force push (--force) → will break history


do NOT reset → you’ll lose your checkpoint

main updated → yes


tag exists remotely → yes


UI checkpoint preserved → yes

Im having issues to get builder running properly: ## Error Type
Build Error

## Error Message
Module parse failed: Unexpected token (1:7)

## Build Output
./node_modules/esbuild/lib/main.d.ts
Module parse failed: Unexpected token (1:7)
> export type Platform = 'browser' | 'node' | 'neutral'
| export type Format = 'iife' | 'cjs' | 'esm'
| export type Loader = 'base64' | 'binary' | 'copy' | 'css' | 'dataurl' | 'default' | 'empty' | 'file' | 'js' | 'json' | 'jsx' | 'local-css' | 'text' | 'ts' | 'tsx'

Next.js version: 15.5.12 (Webpack)

Current task: Stop esbuild from breaking the build (UI must run)

Reality (no fluff)
You’re stuck in a loop because:


Next 15 WILL try to bundle esbuild


esbuild contains .d.ts inside runtime path


Webpack cannot parse that


Your preview route is poisoning the entire app build


You tried:


dynamic import ❌


require ❌


serverExternalPackages ❌


→ All still let webpack touch esbuild

Correct move (for NOW): REMOVE esbuild from runtime path
You said:

AI / preview logic is NOT part of this task

So stop letting it break the UI.

Bash — HARD STABILIZATION (copy/paste)
1. Replace preview route with safe stub
Bashcat <<'EOF' > app/api/dev/preview/route.ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";

export const runtime = "nodejs";

export async function GET(req: NextRequest) {
  const { searchParams } = new URL(req.url);
  const projectId = searchParams.get("projectId");

  if (!projectId) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "Missing projectId" }, { status: 400 });
  }

  // 🔒 STABLE MODE: disable esbuild completely
  return NextResponse.json({
    ok: true,
    projectId,
    mode: "stub-preview"
  });
}
EOF

2. Clean + restart
Bashrm -rf .next
npm run dev

Expected result (must be YES)


builder loads → yes


no .d.ts error → yes


filetree works → yes


editor works → yes


preview no longer crashes → yes


Preview will NOT render real output → this is intentional

Why this is the correct move
You are in Builder Core stabilization phase, not preview engine phase.
Right now:


UI = priority ✅


Preview engine = separate module ❌


You isolate the failure instead of letting it break everything.

When to bring esbuild back
Later, do it properly via:


separate worker


or edge function


or external service


NOT inside Next route.

Lock this state
Bashgit add app/api/dev/preview/route.ts
git commit -m "stabilize(preview): stub preview to unblock builder UI (esbuild isolated)"
git push origin main

Task complete.
